decision: Two alternatives, as KerML 8.2.4.1.6 states them. The distinction between them is the `member` keyword that TypeFeatureMember carries and OwnedFeatureMember does not, and that keyword is the whole of the concrete-syntax difference.
notes:
re-scoped from the shared unit to kerml alone (ADR-0015); awaiting grammar_check_unit.py against this language's grammar alone
The clause and the Xtext agree exactly.

FOR A PARSER AUTHOR: the two alternatives are distinguishable, but not at the first token, because both open with the nullable MemberPrefix. The decision point is the token after the optional visibility indicator: `member` selects TypeFeatureMember, anything that can start a FeatureElement selects OwnedFeatureMember. The two are otherwise the same shape.

WHY THE DISTINCTION EXISTS, as far as this production says: the clause gives the two alternatives different metaclasses — TypeFeatureMember is an OwningMembership, OwnedFeatureMember is a FeatureMembership — so the keyword changes which relationship the member establishes. That is abstract syntax and belongs to whoever builds the element; recorded here only because it is why one keyword is worth a production.

The empty corpus_instances is expected: this is a pure alternation contributing no terminal of its own, so corpus text is attributable to whichever alternative matched.

evidence.note: FeatureMember is stated there as TypeFeatureMember | OwnedFeatureMember
